plan.container.restart: Restart container {name}; its services blip briefly
plan.container.stop: Stop container {name}. Its services are unavailable until it starts again
plan.cron.add_script: Add job "{name}": run a script as {what} on {cron}
plan.cron.update_script: Change job "{name}": run a script as {what} on {cron}
plan.db.drop: Drop database {name} in {instance}; a copy is exported to /srv/berth/backups/db-drops/ first
plan.db.exec: Run the statement below on {db} in {instance} (changes data; cannot be undone)
plan.db.exec_danger_drop: Danger: the statement drops a database, table, user or column ({instance} / {db}); cannot be undone
plan.db.exec_danger_no_where: Danger: DELETE / UPDATE without WHERE affects the whole table ({instance} / {db})
plan.db.exec_danger_truncate: Danger: the statement empties a whole table ({instance} / {db}); cannot be undone
plan.db.import: Import {path} into {db} on {instance} (the current data is saved first, so it can be undone)
plan.db.instance.remove: Stop managing {name} here (the database itself is untouched)
plan.db.native.allow_none: {name}: this server and its containers only
plan.db.native.install: Install {engine} {version} natively on the server and register it
plan.db.remote_all: {name} listens on port {port} on every address; anyone who can reach this machine can try to log in
plan.db.remote_lan: {name} listens on {addr}:{port}; machines on that network can connect
plan.db.remote_off: {name} listens on this server only (127.0.0.1:{port}); remote access off
plan.db.root_reset: Reset the password of {user} on {instance} (the old one is not needed)
plan.db.slowlog_on: Slow query log on for {name}: statements over {seconds} s
plan.db.sqlite.restore: Put backup {backup} back over {name} (the current file is backed up first)
plan.db.sqlite.wal: Switch {name} to WAL mode (backed up first)
plan.db.tune: Tune {name} and restart it (the old settings come back if it does not start)
plan.db.user.create: Create user {user} in {instance} with rights on {db}
plan.ddns.set: Keep {name} pointing at this server ({type}, now {ip}, from {source}), checked every 5 minutes
plan.ddns.update: Public address changed: {name} moved from {before} to {ip}
plan.desktop.disable: Stop the desktop and keep it from starting at boot (software stays; turn it on again any time)
plan.desktop.enable: Start the desktop as {user}, listening on 127.0.0.1:{port} only; a generated password goes into the connection library
plan.desktop.install: Install the desktop and {n} software groups (about {mb} MB); only newly installed packages are recorded and removed on uninstall
plan.desktop.uninstall: Stop the desktop and remove the packages Berth installed; the berthdesk user and its files stay
plan.dev.claude_auth.api_key: Give Claude in {name} an API key (kept sealed)
plan.dev.claude_auth.login: Claude in {name} uses the account you sign in with inside it (the panel keeps no key)
plan.dev.claude_auth.token: Give Claude in {name} a sign-in token (kept sealed)
plan.dev.claude_update: Download the newest Claude Code (one copy for every workspace; used from their next start)
plan.dev.create: Create dev workspace {name} ({cpus} CPU, {mem} MB memory)
plan.dev.delete: Delete dev workspace {name}; the project folder {dir} stays
plan.dev.delete_files: Delete dev workspace {name} and move {dir} to the trash
plan.dev.rebuild: Rebuild dev workspace {name} from its current configuration: project files and /home stay, anything installed elsewhere in the container is lost
plan.dev.set: Change dev workspace {name} ({cpus} CPU, {mem} MB); the container restarts
plan.dev.task_cancel: Stop task #{id} in {name} (files it already changed stay; you can take them back from its result)
plan.dev.task_revert: Put the files in {name} back to how they were before task #{id} (refused, not overwritten, where they changed since)
plan.disk.cleanup_buildcache: Delete unused build cache (the next build is slower)
plan.disk.cleanup_images: Delete untagged images no container uses
plan.disk.cleanup_journal: Keep the system journal to 14 days and 200 MB
plan.disk.format: Format {dev} as {fs} — everything on it is lost for good
plan.disk.mount_boot: Mount {dev} at {path}, also at boot (written to /etc/fstab; a missing disk will not stop the boot)
plan.disk.unmount: Unmount {path} ({dev}) and stop mounting it at boot
plan.docker.login: Log in to {registry} as {user} (the password goes to Docker only)
plan.docker.logs: New containers keep at most {files} log files of {size} each (existing ones after they are recreated)
plan.drift.accept: Take {path} as it is now as Berth's version
plan.drift.restore: Put Berth's version of {path} back (the current one is kept as .external)
plan.edge.connect: Connect {container} to berth-edge so Caddy can reach it by name
plan.edge.install: Start Caddy ({image}) on this host on ports 80/443; every site is served through it. The first run builds the image here and takes a few minutes
plan.edge.stop: Stop Caddy: every site on this host goes offline (config and certificates are kept)
plan.edge.upgrade: Upgrade the site gateway from {from} to {to}: rebuild the Caddy image here (a few minutes), then recreate the container; sites pause for a few seconds
plan.ext.av.install: Download ClamAV and its signatures (about 560 MB; the system is not changed)
plan.ext.av.remove: Delete the ClamAV image and its signatures
plan.ext.install: Install "{name}" ({id}) with {n} granted scopes; it can do only those, and everything it does is audited
plan.ext.remove: Remove "{name}": revoke its token and stop its container
plan.ext.waf.install: Add the WAF (Coraza + OWASP CRS) to the site edge; sites pause for a few seconds
plan.ext.waf.remove: Remove the WAF: turn it off on {n} sites and go back to the edge without it (undo restores them)
plan.file.purge: Permanently delete {count} items from the trash; this cannot be undone
plan.file.share: Make a public download link for {path}, valid {hours} h (limit {max} downloads, 0 = none)
plan.file.share_pw: Make a password-protected download link for {path}, valid {hours} h (limit {max}, 0 = none)
plan.file.trash: Move {count} items to the trash (can be restored)
plan.file.write_large: Save {path} ({size}). The old file is over 2 MB, so no copy is kept and this cannot be undone
plan.firewall.confirm: Keep the pending firewall changes and make them permanent
plan.firewall.rollback: Restore the firewall as it was before the pending changes
plan.firewall.rule.delete: Remove firewall rule: {rule}. Rolls back in 60 s unless confirmed
plan.firewall.rule.delete_lockout: Warning: afterwards YOU cannot reach {lockout}. Remove firewall rule: {rule}
plan.firewall.rule.set: Firewall: {rule}. Rolls back in 60 s unless confirmed
plan.firewall.rule.set_lockout: Warning: this cuts YOU off from {lockout}. Firewall: {rule}. Rolls back in 60 s unless confirmed
plan.host.agent_update: Upgrade {name}'s agent from {from} to {to} (rolls back on its own if the new one does not reconnect)
plan.host.enroll: Host {name} joined the panel with a join code
plan.host.join_code: Create a one-time join code for host {name}, valid for 30 minutes
plan.host.remove: Remove host {name}: disconnect its agent and revoke its key (services on it keep running)
plan.image.prune: Delete {count} untagged, unused images, freeing about {size}
plan.integration.delete: Delete DNS account {id} (records at the provider stay)
plan.integration.set: Save DNS account {id} ({kind}); the credentials were checked
plan.invite.create: Create an invitation ({preset}, up to {n} people, valid {days} days)
plan.link.accept: Hand {hosts} to the main panel "{name}" (waiting for it to confirm)
plan.link.active: Main panel "{name}" confirmed and now manages the servers handed over
plan.link.code: Make a panel link code (15 minutes, single use)
plan.link.confirm: Confirm the panel link: manage {hosts} of "{name}"
plan.migrate.code: Create a migration code (valid 24 hours; whoever has it can read the data this host would move)
plan.migrate.folders: Take {n} extra folders along when moving
plan.migrate.import: Move in {n} items from {from}, about {size}. Data is written to its final place as it arrives; no big pack is stored first
plan.native.create: Create native project {name} (settings only; deploy next)
plan.native.delete: Delete native project {name}: stop it; its code and data stay
plan.native.deploy: Deploy a new release of {name}: built and checked before it takes over; the current one serves until then
plan.native.update: Change native project {name}'s settings (used from the next deploy)
plan.panel.restore: Replace this panel's database, keys and certificates with the snapshot ({detail}). The panel restarts and you sign in again; the current data stays in *.before-restore-<time>
plan.panel.rolled_back: Updating to {to} failed and was rolled back to {from}: {detail}
plan.panel.snapshot: Export a panel snapshot (database, keys, certificates; password-sealed)
plan.panel.update: Update the panel and agent from {from} to {to}. A backup is taken first; if the new version is not up within 60 s, the old one is restored. Sites and containers are not affected.
plan.panel.update_web: Update the web UI from {from} to {to} (no restart)
plan.panel.web_reset: Stop serving the downloaded UI and go back to the one built into Berth {version}
plan.php.native.install: Install PHP {version} natively (beside any other PHP; the system's own is untouched)
plan.php.set: PHP {version}: build the runtime with {n} extensions (a few minutes the first time)
plan.pipeline.delete: Delete pipeline {name} (run and release history stay; released services keep running)
plan.pkg.remove: Remove {names} ({n} packages, including dependencies no longer needed)
plan.plugin.install_root: Install plugin {name} {version}, running as root, with {n} Berth permissions
plan.plugin.remove: Remove plugin {name} and revoke its token
plan.plugin.upgrade: Update plugin {name} to {version} (data kept) with {n} Berth permissions
plan.plugin.upgrade_root: Update root plugin {name} to {version} with {n} Berth permissions
plan.project.create: Create project {name} ({kind}): starts at boot, restarts on crash
plan.project.delete: Stop and delete project {name} (its files stay)
plan.proxy.install: Run the Xray container ({image}, host network); manage nodes and users on the Proxy page
plan.proxy.node.delete: Delete node "{name}"; its users lose this node
plan.proxy.node.set: Save node "{name}" ({protocol}, port {port}); rebuild the config and restart Xray
plan.proxy.settings: Change the proxy's link address and restrictions
plan.proxy.uninstall: Stop and remove the Xray container; nodes and users are kept for a reinstall
plan.proxy.user.delete: Delete proxy user "{name}"; their subscription stops working
plan.proxy.version: Xray {from} → {to}: download and restart; people online drop for a few seconds
plan.pve.delete: The panel forgets "{name}" (nothing changes on the PVE side)
plan.pve.power.stop: Power off {name} at once (unsaved data is lost)
plan.pve.rollback: Roll {name} back to "{snapshot}": everything since is lost, and it cannot be undone
plan.pve.set: Connect Proxmox VE "{name}" ({url}); the token is checked before it is saved
plan.pve.snapshot_delete: Delete snapshot "{snapshot}" of {name} (no going back to it afterwards)
plan.raid.add: Add {dev} to {array} (it is wiped, then the array rebuilds)
plan.raid.create_btrfs: Build a Btrfs {level} file system {name} from {devs} — their data is lost
plan.raid.create_md: Build {level} array {name} from {devs} — their data is lost
plan.raid.delete: Stop and dismantle {array} — its data can no longer be read
plan.raid.scrub: Check all of {target} (runs in the background)
plan.rd.connection.restore: Put the remote connection back as it was
plan.rd.install: Deploy the guacd container (listening on 127.0.0.1:4822 only) so the panel can open RDP / VNC / SSH in the browser
plan.registry.install: Run the registry {addr} here (certificate from the panel's CA, generated password) and make every managed host trust and log in to it
plan.registry.prune: Delete {count} old image tags and reclaim space (the newest per repository, images in use and hand-pushed tags stay)
plan.registry.remove: Stop the registry {addr}; stored images stay in /srv/berth/registry/data
plan.release.deploy: Switch {service} on {host} from {before} to {after}; it goes back automatically if the health check fails
plan.sftp.create: Create SFTP account {name} that sees only {dir} (read and write)
plan.sftp.create_ro: Create SFTP account {name} that sees only {dir} (read only)
plan.sftp.delete: Delete SFTP account {name} (the files in {dir} stay)
plan.site.cms_blank: Create {domain}'s directory with a test page (phpinfo)
plan.site.cms_discuz: Install the Discuz! X3.5 forum on {domain}, with a database and user on {db} (enter them in its installer)
plan.site.cms_typecho: Put Typecho on {domain} and create its database on {db} (enter it on the install page)
plan.site.cms_wordpress: Put WordPress on {domain}: create its database on {db} and write wp-config.php
plan.site.delete: Delete {domain}: it stops being served (its target keeps running)
plan.site.disable: Disable {domain}: requests will no longer be answered
plan.site.fix_perms: Give {domain}'s files to the PHP user; directories 755, files 644
plan.site.tamper_on: Turn on tamper protection for {domain}: its files are locked, even against root and PHP (except the listed directories)
plan.ssh.confirm: Keep the new SSH settings and cancel the automatic restore
plan.ssh.key_add: Let a key log in as {user} ({comment})
plan.ssh.key_remove: Stop this key from logging in as {user}: {fp}
plan.ssh.rollback: Put the previous SSH settings back now
plan.ssh.set: Change the SSH server settings; they revert by themselves unless you keep them within {secs} s
plan.ssh.set_port: Move SSH to port {port} (SELinux and the firewall are opened for it); connect on the new port once, then keep it — otherwise it reverts after {secs} s
plan.statuspage.set: Public status page /status/{slug} with {count} checks (names and up/down only)
plan.swap.set: Change swap (rebuilding zram first moves what is in it out, which can take a while)
plan.sync.set: Sync {path} to {target}:{target_path} on schedule ({cron}), and once now
plan.sync.set_delete: Mirror {path} to {target}:{target_path} on schedule ({cron}): files deleted here are deleted there too
plan.sysctl.set: Change {n} kernel parameters (now and at boot)
plan.system.auto_updates_all: Install all updates daily from {time} (never restarts by itself)
plan.system.auto_updates_security: Install security updates daily from {time} (never restarts by itself)
plan.system.net_confirm: The network works: keep the new settings
plan.system.net_rollback: Put the previous network settings back now
plan.system.nic: Change {name}; it goes back by itself unless confirmed within {secs} s
plan.system.nic_default: Change the main card {name} (default route; the panel may be reached through it); it goes back by itself unless confirmed within {secs} s
plan.system.power_cancel: Cancel the scheduled restart / power off
plan.system.poweroff: Power off {host} in {minutes} minutes (it can only be turned on at the machine)
plan.system.reboot: Restart {host} in {minutes} minutes (the panel and every service pause meanwhile)
plan.system.service_disable: Stop {name} and do not start it at boot
plan.system.signal_kill: Force {name} (PID {pid}) to stop; unsaved data is lost
plan.system.snapshot.create: Snapshot the system (root and /boot); it only takes up what changes afterwards
plan.system.snapshot.delete: Delete system snapshot {id}; you cannot roll back to it afterwards
plan.system.snapshot.delete_previous: Delete {name}, the system kept by a rollback, to free its space

plan.system.snapshot.undo: Undo the rollback to {id} and keep the current system
plan.sysuser.create: Add system user {name} (with a home directory)
plan.sysuser.create_admin: Add system user {name} with administrator rights (sudo)
plan.sysuser.delete_home: Delete system user {name} and {home} (cannot be undone)
plan.token.revoke: Revoke token {name} ({prefix}…). Scripts and AI using it stop working immediately
plan.token.rotate: Rotated token {name}; the old one is revoked (new {prefix}…)
plan.traffic.limit.set: {container}: up {up} kbit/s, down {down} kbit/s (0 = unlimited), {quota} GB a month (0 = none)
plan.traffic.tools.install: Install tc (for limits) and turn on per-connection byte counting
plan.user.password: Reset {username}'s password and sign out all their sessions
plan.vm.create_ct: Create system container {name} ({image}, {cpus} CPU / {mem} MB / {disk} GB) with SSH and your keys
plan.vm.create_ct_lan: Create system container {name} ({image}, {cpus} CPU / {mem} MB / {disk} GB) on the LAN ({port}), its address from the router; with SSH
plan.vm.create_vm: Create virtual machine {name} ({image}, {cpus} CPU / {mem} MB / {disk} GB) with SSH and your keys
plan.vm.create_vm_lan: Create virtual machine {name} ({image}, {cpus} CPU / {mem} MB / {disk} GB) on the LAN ({port}), its address from the router; with SSH
plan.vm.delete: Delete {name} with its disk and {snapshots} snapshots; cannot be undone
plan.vm.forward_remove: Remove forward of host {proto} port {host} to {name}

plan.vm.kill: Power off {name} at once (like pulling the plug)
plan.vm.network_lan: {name} joins the LAN on {parent} with an address from the router; {n} port forwards removed
plan.vm.resize: Set {name} to {cpus} CPU / {mem} MB (disk only grows: {disk} GB)
plan.vm.resize_restart: Set {name} to {cpus} CPU / {mem} MB; a running VM picks it up after a restart
plan.vm.restore: Restore {name} to {snapshot} (the current state is snapshotted first, so this can be undone)
plan.vm.screen_enable: Give {name} a screen (like PVE's console, boot included); restarts it once if running
plan.volume.remove: Delete volume {name}; its data is gone for good
plan.wharf.alerts_berth: Wharf hands its alerts to Berth's channels
plan.wharf.alerts_both: Each side sends its own alerts
plan.wharf.alerts_wharf: Wharf sends Berth's alerts; Berth stops sending them itself
plan.wharf.ddns.claim_berth: Berth keeps {domain}'s DDNS; Wharf shows it read-only
plan.wharf.ddns.claim_wharf: Wharf keeps {domain}'s DDNS (the router knows the public IP best)

system.protected: Stopping this would cut you off from the server or the panel ({why}); refused
system.resolver_unmanaged: This host does not use systemd-resolved; set DNS on the network card instead
system.sftp_conf_changes_root: The SFTP settings would change how other users log in; put back, nothing changed
system.sftp_dir_denied: That directory cannot be shared (a system directory or the panel's own data)
system.sftp_no_login: A new account needs a password or at least one public key
system.sftp_no_sshd: The SSH server is not installed on this machine
system.sftp_user_exists: A system user with that name already exists; pick another name
system.ssh_no_method: Password and key login cannot both be off — nobody could log in
system.ssh_overridden: Another file in sshd_config overrides these settings, so they would not take effect; nothing was changed
system.ssh_pending: The previous SSH change still waits for you to keep or restore it
system.ssh_socket: SSH here is started by ssh.socket; its port is set there, which the panel does not change yet
tasks.interrupted: The panel restarted while this task ran. Run it again
tasks.wait_heavy: Waiting for the heavy task ahead of it (one at a time)
tasks.wait_memory: Memory is tight ({need} MB wanted, {avail} MB free). Waiting at most {max} minutes, then going ahead
terminal.no_default_user: No default terminal user is set. A super admin can pick one under Settings → General → Terminal
terminal.no_user: There is no user {user} on the server
terminal.not_found: Terminal session not found (it may have ended)
token.bad_ip: {value} is not a valid IP or CIDR
token.invalid: The token is invalid, expired, or revoked
token.ip_denied: This token may not be used from {ip}
token.rate_limited: This token is making too many calls. Slow down
token.readonly: This token is read-only and cannot make changes
totp.already_on: An authenticator is already on. Turn it off first to replace it
traffic.no_limit: No limits set for this container
traffic.no_package_manager: No dnf on this host to install with
traffic.no_tc: tc is not installed; install the traffic tools first
update.bad_checksum: The download failed its checksum and was discarded
update.bad_signature: The update manifest's signature is wrong; refused
update.bad_url: The update source must start with https://
update.disabled: This build has no update key; online updates are off
update.no_package: The update has no package for {arch}
update.no_web_override: The built-in UI is already in use
update.watchdog_failed: Could not start the update watchdog; restored the old version: {detail}
upload.not_finished: The file is not fully uploaded, or is the wrong kind
upload.not_found: That upload is gone (uploads are cleared after two days)
upload.offset: Wrong position: the server has {received} bytes
uptime.bad_check: Bad check: name required, HTTP needs http(s)://, TCP needs host:port, interval 30–3600 s
uptime.bad_page: Status page address: lowercase letters, digits and dashes; title required
uptime.not_found: Check or status page not found
user.bad_perm: Unknown permission {perm}, or it is reserved for super admins
user.bad_role: Role must be super admin, admin, or viewer
user.last_super: This is the last super admin; it cannot be demoted or disabled
user.password_long: Passwords can be at most {max} characters
user.password_weak: A password cannot be one character repeated
vm.bad_name: Names use lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter
vm.bad_password: The password needs at least 8 characters on one line
vm.bad_size: Bad size (VMs need at least 512 MB; disks at least 2 GB)
vm.bad_ssh_key: That does not look like an SSH public key (one line starting with ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa or ecdsa-)
vm.no_kvm: No KVM here: system containers only
vm.no_password: No stored password (it uses your SSH keys)
vm.no_screen: {name} has no screen yet: turn it on first (restarts once)
vm.no_vm_image: {image} has no ARM virtual-machine image; use a system container
vm.not_installed: Virtualization is not set up on this host
vm.not_vm: This is a container, it has no screen; use the shell
vms.incus_stuck: incus is not answering (nothing in 20 seconds); its daemon may be stuck. The VMs themselves usually keep running — restart incus under System → Services, or run systemctl restart incus
waf.not_installed: The WAF extension is not installed; install it under Extensions first
wharf.already_paired: Already paired with a Wharf; unpair first
wharf.bad_code: Pairing code invalid or expired; start again
wharf.bad_url: Use https://host[:port] for Wharf and confirm its fingerprint
wharf.link_broken: The Wharf link stopped working; pair again ({detail})
wharf.no_target: This server was not chosen as a mapping target when pairing; pair again or add it in Wharf
wharf.not_published: This site is not published through Wharf
